correctness.rationale: The polar is determined by \(y_i\le1\) and \(\sum_i\max(0,-y_i)\le1\); its enumerated extreme normals give the complete facet system. Difference-facet opposites force \(r\le1/\sqrt2\) and equality of all center coordinates. For centers \(a\mathbf1\), inequalities reduce to \(g_a(s)=(s-1)a+\sqrt{(s+1)/2}\le1\) and \(h_a(d)=da+\sqrt{d/2}\le1\). The \(s=0\) and \(s=2\) facets give the exact endpoints; \(a_++1/(2\sqrt6)=1-5\sqrt6/12<0\) proves that all higher-index facets and the all-ones facet are strictly redundant at admissible \(a\). Hence the entire nonempty segment is feasible and the tangency counts are exhaustive. Exact computational checks through dimension seven corroborate, but do not prove, the universal quantifier.

value.rationale: A natural mixed chain–antichain family emphasized in recent facet-growth literature has exponentially many facets but a universal Euclidean inradius and a dimension-independent, nonunique scalar incenter interval. Its entire contact-facet active-set stratification, including different endpoint jumps, is determined and explains a growing \(\sqrt{d/2}\) advantage over the reflexive origin-centered ball. This supplies a concrete geometric invariant and equality classification not described by the older facet/volume census; no generic polytope calculation or known table immediately states this structure.
